fatal_errors: The proposed TiB2-Ag-MoS2 ceramic is not the target CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 high-entropy-alloy composite.
It omits the varied Mo content, Mo-induced FCC lattice distortion, and hard sigma-phase formation central to the intervention and strengthening mechanism.
The processing route and parameters are invented and conflict with the target spark-plasma-sintering procedure.
The quantitative friction and wear predictions have no cited evidence and do not reproduce the target's strongly nonmonotonic temperature dependence.
The high-temperature NiO and silver-molybdate glaze mechanism is absent.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses wide-temperature self-lubrication and includes Ag and MoS2, so it has limited conceptual alignment with low-temperature lubrication in the target. However, it substitutes an entirely different TiB2 matrix, composition, baseline, fabrication process, and test protocol. It also misses the key role of Mo variation in lattice distortion and sigma-phase strengthening and does not describe the oxide/silver-molybdate glaze responsible for performance at 600–800 °C. The proposed COF and wear reductions and acceptance thresholds are unsupported. The reciprocating wear test is somewhat falsifiable, but it lacks the phase, microstructure, mechanical, and tribofilm measurements needed to discriminate the target mechanism.
